abstract_snippet: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks in an encoder-decoder configuration. We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.

paper_title: Solving Mixed Integer Programs Using Neural Networks
abstract_snippet: Mixed integer linear programming is a foundational optimization framework. We propose a hybrid approach using bipartite Graph Convolutional Networks to parameterize two key algorithmic subroutines: Neural Diving to predict partial variable assignments, and Neural Branching to select branching variables.

paper_title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
abstract_snippet: Deeper neural networks are more difficult to train. We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously. We explicitly reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, instead of learning unreferenced functions.

paper_title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
abstract_snippet: We introduce Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions, based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments. The method is straightforward to implement, is computationally efficient, has little memory requirements, and is invariant to diagonal rescaling of the gradients.

We propose a novel family of policy gradient methods for reinforcement learning, which alternate between sampling data through interaction with the environment, and optimizing a surrogate objective function using stochastic gradient ascent. We introduce a clipped surrogate objective that prevents destructively large policy updates.

paper_title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
abstract_snippet: An important paradigm of natural language processing involves large-scale pre-training on general domain data and adaptation to specific tasks. We propose Low-Rank Adaptation, or LoRA, which freezes the pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the Transformer architecture.
